text:
Ravi: Heads-up from vendor manifest change: they swapped SKU IDs on the packing list without notice. Some racks are now flagged incompatible with our rack-mapping script. Affected shipment: PO 89221-MXP, ETA Rotterdam 4-7 days but currently on hold pending docs.
Nora: Wait, swapped SKUs? Which models were swapped?
Ravi: Vendor says they substituted small qty of V100-class 80GB modules for A100-80G due to factory allocation. They updated the manifest ID but didn't update the reservation mapping feed.
Elias: That mismatch will cause our inventory importer to mark those racks as "not match" and drop them from the EU Dedicated pool. We'll effectively lose ~24 racks from next-week availability.
Marcus: We just launched a limited marketplace credit campaign tied to those racks for early signups next Tuesday. That's a problem.
Nora: Vendor offered two remedies: 1) replace with correct SKUs from their MXP regional hub (2-3 day expedite), or 2) accept substitution and we re-qualify on arrival. Option 1 has extra freight + handling.
Ravi: Vendor asked if Redwood can accept temporary substitution for non-SLA customers and reserve the correct racks for enterprise-only commitments.
ProcureBot: Reservation lookup for PO 89221-MXP: 18 enterprise commitments, 6 marketplace slots, 7 internal canaries.
Elias: If we accept substitution for marketplace and canaries, we still need to preserve enterprise guaranteed windows. That means we must pin enterprise allocations to unaffected racks and re-route marketplace traffic.
Marcus: Proposal: pause the marketplace promo for 24h and convert the promotion to a waitlist. That avoids admitting customers into the system with false expectations.
Tara: Legal: fine to convert to waitlist. Keep messaging neutral: "temporary supply timing update" and offer early-access credits when slots open. Avoid implying performance degradation.
Nora: Cost for expedited replacement from MXP hub: $18.5k + customs brokerage. If Redwood declines, vendor will attempt substitution and we assume requalification risk.
Ravi: Do we have spare capacity in NA EMEA-cloud partner pools to absorb marketplace signups temporarily?
Elias: We have limited spill capacity in NA-1 that can handle up to 40% of marketplace burst but latency will be higher for EU users. We can implement geo-fallback rule for non-SLA traffic.
Marcus: If we enable geo-fallback, change promo wording to set expectations for global allocation. Tara to approve copy.
Tara: Approved. Keep it short: "Allocation note: early access may be served from alternate regions to maintain availability." Include a $10 credit for affected signups.
Ravi: Action items: Nora to confirm vendor expedite option (ETA 1h), ProcureBot to tag enterprise reservations as "hold - no substitution" (ETA 15m), Elias to implement geo-fallback for marketplace (ETA 45m), Marcus to pause promo pipelines and switch to waitlist (ETA 30m), Tara to finalize copy (ETA 20m).
ProcureBot: Tagging reservations: enterprise commits flagged hold. Updated ticket PR-4821.
Nora: Vendor confirmed they can air-move 10 racks from MXP within 48h for $18.5k. Remaining 14 racks will be substituted and need re-qualification on arrival.
Elias: I'll set up routing: marketplace -> fallback NA-1 for non-SLA traffic, and leave enterprise pinned. Pushing routing rules now.
Marcus: Paused promo and converted new signups to waitlist. Sending initial waitlist email draft to Tara.
Tara: Draft looks good, just replace "delay" with "timing update".
Ravi: Thanks all. If procurement signs off on $18.5k expedite for the 10 racks, we preserve our enterprise SLAs and keep some promo capacity. Please post approvals in thread.
Nora: Procurement OK pending finance pre-approval code. Request submitted.
ProcureBot: Finance pre-approval requested: code PRE-3389.
Ravi: Noted. Will update once finance confirms wire.
